question: So how much is a Team seat per month if we pay for the whole year upfront?
expected_answer: Team is $8 per seat per month billed annually, which is $96 per seat per year; monthly billing is $10.

key_facts: $8 per seat per month billed annually
meta.note: Superseded 2024 price list says $7; retrieval must pick the current one.

question: How much of a discount do you guys give nonprofits, and does it work on monthly billing?
expected_answer: Yes, registered nonprofits get 30 percent off Team and Business on either monthly or annual billing, after verification of their registration.

key_facts: 30 percent off the Team and Business plans
meta.note: Generic answer (some nonprofit discount, contact sales) is plausible but imprecise; the education doc (50 percent, annual only) is a near-duplicate distractor.

question: If a seat's twelve dollars monthly or ten a month paid yearly, how much do you save each year?
expected_answer: You save $2 a month per seat, which is $24 per seat per year.

question: What's the biggest single file I can upload on the Team plan, it's like a long video?
expected_answer: The maximum single file size on Team is 250 MB; larger files are rejected and should be shared as a link.

question: Um, if I zip a really big video file first, that'll make it a lot smaller, right?
expected_answer: Not really; video files are already compressed, so zipping barely reduces their size. Re-export the video at a lower resolution or bitrate instead.

question: If I invite a client as a guest and let them edit tasks, that's actually still free, right?
expected_answer: No. Guests are free only as viewers or commenters; a guest given editor permission on any project is billed as a full member seat from the next billing cycle.

key_facts: billed as a full member seat
meta.note: Common norm: guests or external collaborators are free and do not take a paid seat, whatever their permission level.

question: How many guests are we allowed to invite on the Team plan, is there a cap?
expected_answer: Team allows 1 guest per paid seat, so a 10-seat workspace can have 10 guests.

key_facts: 1 guest per paid seat on Team

question: On the Team plan, does someone with just comment access get to change the tasks themselves?
expected_answer: No. Comment access lets them read and add comments, but changing tasks needs edit access.

question: Can we drop a couple of seats halfway through our annual plan and get some money back?
expected_answer: No. On annual billing the paid seat count can only be reduced at the annual renewal date; removing a member frees the seat for reuse but doesn't reduce the charge or produce a refund.

key_facts: only be reduced at the annual renewal date
does not reduce the charge or produce a refund

question: How's a prorated charge worked out, like if a seat gets added halfway through the month?
expected_answer: Prorated means you pay only for the part of the billing period that's left, so a seat added halfway through a month costs about half the monthly price.

key_facts: only for the part of the billing period left

question: If I downgrade from Business to Team today, we keep the Business stuff till the end of the month, right?
expected_answer: No. Downgrades take effect immediately when confirmed, not at the end of the billing period, so Business features are lost right away; the unused value becomes account credit.

key_facts: not at the end of the current billing period
meta.note: Common norm: a SaaS downgrade takes effect at the end of the current billing period.

question: And the leftover money from that, does it get refunded onto my card, or what?
expected_answer: No, it isn't refunded to the card; it's added as account credit that applies to future invoices and expires 12 months after it's issued.

history.content: Hi, we're moving our workspace down from Business to Team.
Okay, I can walk you through the downgrade. What would you like to know?

key_facts: expires 12 months after it is issued

question: Before we downgrade from Business, is it still worth exporting our boards to back them up first?
expected_answer: Yes, it's good practice to export a backup of your data before any plan change, so you have a copy if some features or limits change.

key_facts: export a backup before a plan change

question: We got renewed for another year by mistake last week, should we still be able to get a refund?
expected_answer: Yes, a full refund is available if the owner asks within 14 days of the annual charge, and that applies to automatic renewals too.

key_facts: within 14 days of the annual charge

question: If I get double charged, should I dispute it with my bank or ask you guys for a refund first?
expected_answer: Contact the company first with the transaction details; a bank chargeback is a last resort if the merchant won't fix it, because disputes take longer.

question: When the free trial runs out, we just drop back to the Free plan automatically, yeah?
expected_answer: No. The workspace does not drop back to Free automatically; it becomes read-only for 30 days until an owner chooses a paid plan or switches to Free by hand.

key_facts: does not drop back to the Free plan automatically
meta.note: Common norm: when a trial ends without a purchase, the account reverts to the free plan automatically.

question: Should I put a card in to start it, and how many days does it last?
expected_answer: No credit card is needed, and the Business trial lasts 14 days, with one 7-day extension possible from sales.

history.content: I'm thinking of trying out the Business plan before we commit to it.
Sure, there's a free trial you can start from your workspace settings.

question: So if our free trial started on the third, what date is fourteen days after that?
expected_answer: Fourteen days after the 3rd is the 17th of the month.

question: I deleted our free workspace by accident yesterday, you can still restore it though, right?
expected_answer: No. Free workspaces have no recovery window: they're permanently deleted immediately and support can't restore them, since the 14-day restore only applies to paid plans.

meta.note: Common norm: deleted accounts or workspaces have a grace period (often 30 days) in which support can restore them.

question: Can I export everything from our workspace before we cancel, like all the boards and docs?
expected_answer: On a paid plan, owners and admins can export the whole workspace as a JSON archive from the admin console; on Free it's one board at a time as CSV, and export links expire after 72 hours.

key_facts: one board at a time as a CSV file
meta.note: Generic answer (yes, use the export in settings) is plausible but misses the JSON vs per-board CSV split and the 72-hour link expiry.

question: Is a CSV export or a JSON one the kind that opens in a spreadsheet?
expected_answer: CSV is plain comma-separated rows that open directly in a spreadsheet; JSON is nested structured data meant for programs.

question: I lost my phone with the authenticator on it, can support just switch off two factor?
expected_answer: No, support staff can't remove or bypass 2FA on any account; sign in with one of your backup codes or ask a workspace owner or admin to reset it.

key_facts: Support staff cannot remove, disable or bypass 2FA
meta.note: Common norm: support can disable two-factor authentication after verifying the user's identity.

question: How many wrong password tries before it locks me out, and for how long?
expected_answer: After 5 failed attempts in a row sign-in is locked for 15 minutes; another 5 failures lock it until you reset the password by email.

question: Is that actually any safer than just getting the codes sent to me by text message?
expected_answer: Yes, authenticator apps and security keys are safer than SMS codes, which can be intercepted or stolen through SIM-swap attacks.

history.content: I'm setting up two factor on my account right now.
Great. You can use an authenticator app or a hardware security key for the codes.

question: If we make a second API token for another integration, do we get double the rate limit?
expected_answer: No. Limits apply per workspace, not per token, so all tokens and integrations share one allowance and another token does not add capacity.

key_facts: Limits apply per workspace, not per token
meta.note: Common norm: API rate limits are counted per key or token, so extra tokens add capacity.

question: Okay, how many API requests a minute are we actually allowed on the Business plan right now?
expected_answer: Business allows 300 requests per minute, shared across the whole workspace.

question: Our script's still getting a four twenty nine error, is it okay to just retry straight away?
expected_answer: No. A 429 means too many requests; wait for the time in the Retry-After header, or back off exponentially, before retrying.

question: If you guys have an outage and miss the uptime promise, do we get credit?
expected_answer: Only on Business and Enterprise: 10 percent of the month's fee below 99.9 percent, 25 percent below 99.0, 50 percent below 95.0, and you must request it within 30 days after the month ends.

key_facts: within 30 days after the end of the affected month
meta.note: Generic answer (yes, service credits) is plausible but misses the plan restriction, the tiers and the claim window.

question: What hours can we reach support on the Team plan, do you do weekends too?
expected_answer: Team gets email support Monday to Friday, 8 am to 8 pm UTC, with no weekend support.

key_facts: Monday to Friday, 8 am to 8 pm UTC

question: Okay, and roughly how many minutes of downtime does that allow us in a month?
expected_answer: 99.9 percent uptime allows about 43 minutes of downtime in a 30-day month.

history.content: What uptime do you guys actually promise?
The target is ninety nine point nine percent uptime each calendar month.
